column3: NASB adds “our.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “compassions” as “mercies.”
NASB renders “tribulation” as “affliction” and “through” as “with.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “abound toward us” as “are ours in abundance.”
NASB follows the critical text's order of clauses; “constricted” is rendered “afflicted,” and “endurance” is “patient enduring.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “our” twice and “you are sharers.”
NASB follows the critical text without “to us”; “ignorant” is rendered “unaware,” and “weighed” is “burdened.”
NASB adds “indeed.”
NASB follows the critical text (“will deliver”); “a death” is rendered “a peril of death.”
NASB restructures the verse; “supplication” is rendered “prayers.”
NASB reads “holiness,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “simplicity.” “Boasting” is rendered “proud confidence,” and “more abundantly” is “especially.”
NASB follows the critical text without “even.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our”); “boasting” is rendered “reason to be proud,” and “in part” is “partially.”
NASB renders “a second grace” as “twice receive a blessing.”
NASB renders “to be set forward” as “to be helped on my journey.”
NASB follows the critical text; “did I use levity” is rendered “I was not vacillating,” and it adds “at the same time.”
NASB follows the critical text (“is”); it renders “Faithful is God” as “as God is faithful.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Christ Jesus”).
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “they are” and “our.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB moves “as a pledge” to the end.
NASB reorders the verse.
NASB renders “fellow workers of your joy” as “workers with you for your joy.”
